headline: Nigerian women restore mangrove forests devastated by oil
meta_description: Women in Niger Delta plant 3 million mangroves and restore 190 hectares of swamp forest, bringing marine life back to oil-damaged wetlands.
summary_short: A community-led effort in Nigeria's Niger Delta has planted 3 million mangroves and restored 190 hectares of swamp forest, reviving ecosystems damaged by decades of oil…
body:
Women in Nigeria's Niger Delta have planted 3 million mangroves and restored 190 hectares of swamp forest, bringing fish and crabs back to wetlands devastated by oil pollution.

The restoration work addresses damage from decades of industrial extraction in the region. By replanting native mangrove species across the degraded swamp forest, the project has created conditions for marine life to return to areas where pollution had eliminated these species.

The effort demonstrates how community-led conservation can reverse environmental harm on a significant scale. With 3 million trees now growing and nearly 200 hectares of wetland habitat recovering, the project shows both the depth of damage caused by oil development and the possibility of ecological restoration when local women lead the work.
